ASML: a monopoly in the strongest earnings phase of its history, priced at the bottom of its own ten-year valuation range

Written on 9 November 2026 for Richard. All valuation figures use a share price of 1,407.2 EUR, the 23 October close on which the Financial Analyst's model is built. The shares have since fallen to about 1,250 EUR, which strengthens the valuation argument without changing the fundamentals. The basis of the forecasts and the meaning of each term are in the end notes.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

ASML is the sole supplier of the lithography tool that gates every leading-edge logic and DRAM fab, and the AI build-out has turned that monopoly into a sold-out factory.

  • FY2026 revenue guidance has risen from 34 to 39 billion EUR in January to 44 to 45 billion EUR in October: growth of about 36% against an opening midpoint of about 12%.
  • Long-lead parts fix 2027 output of Low-NA EUV systems at about 85, and that output is close to fully ordered.
  • Orders for 2028 are already in.
  • Customers are pre-paying 35 to 40% of a tool's value to hold their delivery slots.

As a result, ASML's earnings path to FY2028 is the most traceable in the European cyclical universe. EPS roughly triples, from about 25 EUR in FY2025 to about 75 EUR in FY2028. About two-thirds of the increase comes from revenue, where supply caps unit volumes and prices are already signed. About one-third comes from margin, because operating expenses grow at half the rate of revenue. The path needs no financial leverage, and buybacks shrink the share count by about 2% a year.

The case, in one sentence

ASML is a monopoly in the strongest earnings phase of its history, priced at the bottom of its own ten-year valuation range because the market has decided that 2028 is the cycle's peak before the company has disclosed the three numbers that decide whether 2028 is the peak.

Eight conclusions that matter for the decision

  1. The EPS step-up is already in consensus; the re-rating is not. FY2027 consensus EPS has risen 79% in twelve months and FY2028 consensus EPS 106%. Over the same period, ASML's two-year-forward P/E has fallen from about 35x in June 2026 to about 20x, the 2nd percentile of its five-year range. Morgan Stanley's arithmetic states most cleanly what the share price discounts: at 1,250 EUR and a trough multiple of 20x, the market is paying for FY2028 EPS of about 62 EUR. That EPS equates to about 93 Low-NA systems in 2028, flat on 2027, against 110 in our base and 110-plus in consensus. The investment case is therefore a multiple case resting on an earnings floor, not a case that needs an earnings surprise.

  1. Three undisclosed numbers decide 2028, and the market will receive them on two dates. The three numbers are the 2028 Low-NA unit count (above 110 or not), the size of the completed value-based price reset, and the run-rate of near-100%-margin software upgrades once customers' new cleanrooms open. Together they explain about two-thirds of the revenue step from FY2025 to FY2028 and almost all of the margin step. Two of the three are contracted for 2027 (units fixed, prices signed), which is why FY2027 is predictable. None of the three is contracted for 2028, which is why the range of FY2028 outcomes is wide. The resolving events are the Q4 results on 27 January 2027, which carry the first official order backlog since the last reported 38.8 billion EUR (Bernstein infers about 56 billion EUR), and the Capital Markets Day on 10 June 2027, which brings a new 2030 framework, 2028 capacity, the margin path and a new buyback.
  1. The skew of outcomes is favourable near term and unfavourable further out, and the two must be kept apart. For FY2027, the 80% range for EPS is 50 to 61 EUR around a base of 56 EUR. The most likely FY2027 outcome sits slightly above the base, because upgrades and margin have beaten expectations in every quarter of 2026, while policy fattens the left tail. For FY2028, the 80% range is 57 to 87 EUR around 75 EUR and is skewed down: the downside combines volume, mix and policy, while supply caps the upside at about 120 units. For FY2029, our base is a pause (revenue +2.8%), but I put the probability of a decline at about 40%. Every growth run in ASML's history has ended in digestion, and the AI capital spending that drives 2028 to 2029 orders is now partly financed externally.
  1. ASML's reinforcing loops will turn in a known order, and the cash line will turn first. The upgrade-for-cleanroom loop turns first, in late 2027 to 2028, and shows in the mix of installed-base revenue and in gross margin. The loop from customer prepayments to buybacks turns second, in 2029, and shows in contract liabilities, free cash flow and buybacks. Unit volumes turn last. In our base, FY2029 EPS still rises 4% while free cash flow falls about 16% and non-current contract liabilities turn down. No broker models this sequence. The first quarter-on-quarter fall in non-current contract liabilities would make the turn visible at once. The sequence is both the case's early-warning system and the reason the three-year horizon is riskier than the 18-month horizon.
  1. Three dated optical traps sit inside the window, and each is a buying opportunity if the order book holds. The first trap is a conservative opening FY2027 guide on 27 January: following ASML's habit, a midpoint about 4% below consensus revenue is more likely than not, while the same print carries the backlog, the installed-base guide and the Q1 guide, which matter more. The second trap is the seasonal step-down of 10 to 15% in Q1 2027 revenue from Q4 2026. The third trap is reported year-on-year growth falling from about +50% in Q4 2026 to about +8% in Q4 2027, purely because of the high 2026 comparison base, while the sequential run-rate keeps rising. The sector de-rates on optical deceleration and recovers once the deceleration proves optical, as it did in July 2022. ASML's multiple fell 34% in 2017 to 2018, and 21 points of that fall came before any inventory correction.
  2. Policy is the one force that can move revenue by decree; the risk is nearer than the market's framing implies, but milder. The MATCH Act, which would restrict immersion shipments and servicing to designated Chinese fabs, is reportedly in the year-end US defence bill. The suspension of the US Affiliates Rule and China's suspension of its rare-earth measures both expire on 10 November 2026, tomorrow. I size a statutory ban at about 8 to 10% of a full year's EPS, not the roughly 30% Jefferies estimates, because ASML can re-allocate freed immersion tools to other customers while capacity is short. The loss that cannot be re-allocated is Chinese servicing, the highest-margin part of installed-base revenue. The hit grows in a 2029 slowdown, when no other customer is waiting for the freed tools.
  3. The return is large and asymmetric. At Viewforth's guideline fair multiple for a stock in the Reinforcing phase (29.4x, the 90th percentile of ten years), the model's total shareholder return is +70% to March 2028 and +110% to September 2029. The re-rating contributes +46 points at both horizons; earnings contribute +16 points and +42 points. My own central fair multiple is lower, at about 26x, because by March 2028 the market will be looking at a 2029 that we model as flat, and ASML has never held a 90th-percentile multiple into a flat year. At 26x, the 18-month return is about +52%. Earnings alone, with no re-rating, give about +17%. The bear case, a 2029 decline valued at 19x, gives about -13%. The asymmetry is favourable because the multiple has already been through most of a cycle's compression while estimates have not yet peaked.
  4. What would change my mind: observable events in both directions.
    Upward
    • A January backlog above about 55 billion EUR.
    • A 2028 unit number above 115 at the Capital Markets Day.
    • The 10% rise in replacement-parts prices in Korea spreading globally.
    Downward
    • A Q1 2027 installed-base print below about 3.3 billion EUR, or a flat FY2027 installed-base guide: the upgrade loop turning early.
    • Any quarter-on-quarter fall in non-current contract liabilities.
    • A cut of more than 10% to TSMC's 2027 capital spending.
    • Enactment of the MATCH Act with an implementation timetable inside twelve months.

The five judgements that move the shares most, with the arithmetic

The point of this section

Whether 2029 is a pause or a decline moves the shares about three times as much as any other judgement. The 2028 unit count, which dominates the market's debate, is worth less than the upgrade run-rate.

Each judgement is sized against the base (FY2027 EPS 55.9 EUR; FY2028 75.1 EUR; FY2029 78.1 EUR). Each is also sized on the two-year-forward EPS to which the model applies its multiple at the 18-month valuation date, 31 March 2028: about 81.5 EUR, made up of three-quarters FY2029 and one-quarter FY2030. Three conversion rules make the arithmetic quick to follow.

1. 2028 Low-NA units (base 110; plausible range 95 to 120). Each Low-NA system is worth about 0.40 EUR of FY2028 EPS. One system brings about 274 million EUR of revenue at about 65% gross margin with no incremental operating expense: 178 million EUR of EBIT, 147 million EUR after 17.5% tax, or about 0.40 EUR on 369 million shares. Fifteen fewer systems (95) cost about 4.1 billion EUR of revenue and about 6 EUR of FY2028 EPS (-8%); ten more systems (120) add about 2.7 billion EUR of revenue and about 4 EUR of EPS (+5%). The buy side's expectation of 120 to 125 systems is worth 4 to 6 EUR above the base; Morgan Stanley's price-implied 93 systems are worth about 7 EUR below it. Because 2029 units follow 2028 units, the effect on the two-year-forward EPS at March 2028 is of similar size.

2. The upgrade run-rate inside installed-base revenue (base 6.4 billion EUR in 2027, 6.0 billion in 2028, 5.0 billion in 2029). The upgrade run-rate is the largest single source of FY2027 variance and the one with the best early warning. Upgrades carry about 90% gross margin, so one billion EUR of upgrades is about 0.9 billion EUR of gross profit, 0.74 billion EUR after tax and about 2.0 EUR of EPS. If 2028 upgrades fall to Jefferies' implied 3.5 billion EUR as new cleanrooms open, FY2028 EPS loses about 5 EUR (-7%) and group gross margin loses about 2.2 points (Jefferies' 55.2% case). If 2027 upgrades fall to 5.0 billion EUR, FY2027 EPS loses about 2.7 EUR (-5%). The early warnings are the January installed-base guide and the Q1 2027 installed-base print against 3.3 billion EUR.

3. How much of the price reset reaches gross margin (base: about half; FY2028 gross margin 58.3%). About half of the price reset is absorbed before it reaches gross margin. Pricing adds about 2.5 points of gross margin by 2028 against 2026, but capacity-ramp costs, High-NA mix (about 20 to 25% gross margin on early systems) and the normalisation of upgrades absorb about half of that gain. If all of the gain is absorbed, FY2028 gross margin is about 57.0% and EPS about 2 EUR lower (-3%). If all of it flows through (Deutsche Bank's 60% exit rate), EPS is about 2.5 EUR higher. One point of gross margin is worth about 1.2 EUR of FY2027 EPS and about 1.5 EUR of FY2028 EPS. The observable is the FY2027 gross-margin guide: a guide at or below the Q4 2026 exit rate of about 57% would mean capacity costs are eating more than half of the reset.

4. A statutory China ban (the MATCH Act or an equivalent). A full year of a ban costs about 8 to 10% of EPS while capacity is short, and more in a slowdown. China is about 20% of 2026 revenue, falling to about 15% in our 2027 base. With freed immersion tools re-allocated to other customers over seven to twelve months, and about 0.8 billion EUR of Chinese installed-base revenue lost, a full year costs about 4.5 to 5.5 EUR of EPS (-8 to -10%): FY2027 EPS falls to about 52 EUR and FY2028 EPS to about 68 EUR. In a 2029 slowdown, with no re-allocation and under-absorbed capacity, the same ban costs 7 to 9 EUR (-10 to -12%). I put the probability of a ban affecting the P&L inside the 18-month window at about one in six, and in 2028 at about one in three.

5. Is 2029 a pause or a decline (base: revenue +2.8%, gross margin 58.0%, EPS 78.1 EUR)? The 2029 judgement moves the shares more than any other, because it decides both the earnings and the multiple the market will apply to them. In the decline case, revenue falls 12% to about 63 billion EUR, gross margin falls to 56%, and operating expenses cannot fall in the same year. EBIT is then about 27 billion EUR against 33.5 billion EUR in the base, EPS is about 61 to 64 EUR (-18 to -21%), and free cash flow falls well below 0.7x net income as down payments reverse. The two-year-forward EPS at March 2028 falls from about 81.5 EUR to about 64 EUR; at an unchanged 20x, that fall alone is worth about 350 EUR of share price (-25%). I put the probability of a decline at about 40%.

The judgements interact. Judgements 2, 4 and 5 are correlated: a break in memory prices or a freeze in AI financing would cut upgrades first, then DUV and Low-NA units, and would lower the political cost of a China ban in the same year. That correlation is why the FY2028 and FY2029 ranges are skewed down even though each driver alone is roughly symmetrical. Supply caps the upside of judgement 1. If all five go wrong together, the result is Morgan Stanley's full-cycle bear case: FY2028 EPS of 37.5 EUR at 20x, or about 750 EUR a share (-47%). The probability of that case is small but not zero: options in July priced a probability of about 4 to 5% that the shares fall below 750 EUR within a year.

#1 Tailwinds and headwinds in the operating environment

Conclusion: ASML has the strongest fundamental tailwind in the European equipment universe while sitting inside the weakest market regime for its sector. The tailwinds govern earnings to 2028; the headwinds (policy, financing and the discount rate) govern the multiple now and the order book from 2028.

Evidence. The demand change of the last six months is real, because customers' committed capital, not ASML's own words, evidences it. The surge is memory-led: memory system sales are up about 75% in 2026 against about 10% for logic, and the number of EUV exposures per DRAM chip is rising structurally with each node. The headwinds are policy, the financing of AI capital spending, and interest rates.

Inference. The tailwinds act on the 2026 to 2028 earnings line; the headwinds act mainly on the multiple and on the timing of 2028 to 2029 orders. Non-refundable down payments fund 2027 deliveries, so a financing scare changes the multiple first, and changes the 2028 to 2029 order book only if the scare persists into 2027.

Supply, not demand, is the binding constraint, and that constraint has two consequences the market under-weights. First, revenue cannot spike, so, provided orders hold, revenue cannot collapse as sharply as in an unconstrained cycle. Second, ASML's pricing window is longer than in any prior cycle.

So what. The range of forecast outcomes should be narrow for 2026 to 2027 and widen sharply from 2028, which is exactly how the model is built. Over the next six months the headwinds have the upper hand on the share price, because of the sector regime. Over 18 months to four years, the tailwinds govern the operating model.

Counter-case: customers may be over-booking. A supplier of optical components reports customers over-booking by 20 to 30% to secure slots. ASML's controls (down payments with exit costs, orders checked against fab plans, selective acceptance of 2029 to 2030 requests) reduce that risk but do not remove it. The 2021 to 2022 shortage was followed by the 2023 to 2024 digestion. Jefferies models the semiconductor revenue cycle peaking in Q4 2026 on memory-price base effects, and semiconductor-equipment multiples have historically compressed 40 to 50% in the three to six months before the revenue peak.

What would change my view. A TSMC 2027 capital-spending guide in January below about 70 billion USD; a fall in DRAM contract prices below peers' cash cost, which is the trigger for memory capital-spending cuts; or a quarter-on-quarter fall in non-current contract liabilities.

Against the market. I agree with the market that demand visibility is exceptional and that financing is the weak point. I differ on timing: the market is pricing the financing risk into 2027 earnings, which customers have prepaid, when the risk belongs in 2028 to 2029.

88Score: 88, set by the Rater. Committed, customer-prepaid demand reaches nearly all of sales for two to three years: WFE moving from about 160 to above 200 billion USD, TSMC, Micron and Samsung capex sharply up, DRAM EUV layer counts rising structurally, so external forces add most of the +26%/+24% revenue growth to FY2028 (consensus sales growth at the 98th percentile is honest, not a recovery). Net of the direct threats (China falling to about 15% of revenue with MATCH in the defence bill, AI capex now partly externally financed, a 2029 digestion the memo puts at 40%), it sits just under Indra's legislated budget and above Arteche's grid demand; the suddenness of the policy risk is scored in topic 9, not here.

#2 Internally-driven corporate change forces

Conclusion: ASML's internal change forces are strong, broad and unusually well resourced, because customers are financing them. Their 2028 payoff depends on supply-chain execution that management has not yet quantified, and their 2029 payoff depends on a cycle that management cannot control.

Evidence. Five internal changes have happened in 2026, and all five point the same way.

  • Capacity. The strategy has shifted from planning growth to removing the supply constraint. About 30% growth in Low-NA and immersion capacity is committed for 2027 (65 to 85 Low-NA systems; 130 to 170 immersion systems). More than 30% is under investigation for 2028, because management says 30% "will not meet customer demand". Output is now one of the chief executive's two stated daily priorities.
  • Pricing. Value-based pricing negotiations with key customers were completed in Q3. They cover critical products, associated upgrades and services, apply partly in 2027 and fully from 2028, and will not be repeated annually.
  • Installed base. ASML turned the installed base into a "capacity product": customers bought software upgrades (5 to 7% more throughput, at near-100% margin) while waiting for cleanrooms.
  • Buybacks. Buybacks are running at about twice the announced pace, funded by customers' down payments as much as by earnings.
  • People. Leadership is stable through the ramp: the chief executive is in place to 2028, the chief financial officer was reappointed to 2030, and a chief technology officer was added in April 2026. A conditional share award of 20,000 EUR to every eligible employee (about 900 million EUR, vesting January 2030) covers exactly the ramp years.

Inference. The internal forces amplify the external surge and convert it into higher-quality earnings, in three ways.

  • Revenue can grow faster than units from 2027, through price, the mix shift to the NXE:3800F and upgrades.
  • The share count falls faster than consensus assumes. Consensus implies about 376 million shares in FY2028 against our 369 million, so consensus is missing about 2 EUR of EPS.
  • Management is running the business for output rather than for the margin print: the Q4 2026 gross-margin guide is 50 basis points below Q3 on higher revenue, because ramp costs come first.

So what. These forces strengthen the 2026 to 2028 path more than they prove 2029. They are a company's response to an external surge, and at ASML such responses have historically been followed by digestion years. They also carry a cost the market has not counted: the retention award adds about 300 million EUR a year of share-based pay in 2027 to 2029, which roughly cancels the 200 million EUR delayering saving that several brokers credit.

Five negatives are present.

  • Deliberate under-quantification: no 2028 unit number, no pricing percentage, no 2027 margin, and quarterly bookings withdrawn at the peak of order momentum.
  • High-NA economics: about 20% gross margin on early systems, diluting group gross margin by 70 to 100 basis points on four to five recognitions a year.
  • A weaker delayering: negotiated down and deferred to May 2027, during a ramp of more than 30%.
  • Inventory: gross inventories of 12.2 billion EUR at end-2025 carry write-down risk if the build outruns demand.
  • Buybacks at cyclical highs with customers' money: the buyback would be the first thing to reverse.

What would change my view. A 2028 capacity number at or below 110 at the Capital Markets Day (the ambition not converting); a second deferral of the delayering; or installation and application-support constraints showing up as slippage in customers' site acceptance.

Against the market. The market credits the capacity ambition and the price reset and debates their size. It has not priced the retention award, which no sell-side note mentions, and it has not asked what happens to buyback intensity when down payments turn. I agree with Deutsche Bank that investors wanted a clearer route to 60% gross margin and did not get one.

80Score: 80, set by the Rater. The company's own moves are large, funded and already in earnings: about 30% Low-NA and immersion capacity growth committed for 2027 with more under study for 2028, a completed value-based price reset (partial 2027, full 2028), the installed base turned into a near-100%-margin upgrade product, and buybacks at twice the announced pace, with stable leadership and a retention award covering the ramp (the guidance raises themselves are scored in topic 4). Held below the 90 level because these are a response to an external surge rather than an independent programme, the 2028 payoff is unquantified and rests on unproven supply-chain execution, and High-NA dilution, a deferred delayering and the award's cost offset part; close to NKT's funded capacity build but broader, just under Volex's self-made reset.

#3 Value chain, industry structure, business model, financial profile, management

Conclusion: ASML's structure, moat, financial profile and management are each in the top decile of listed European companies. The case's fragilities are not competitive but structural: customer and country concentration, a sole-source supply chain, a policy that can remove a fifth of revenue, and a cash profile that follows customers' down payments.

Industry structure: as supportive as any in the investable universe. ASML holds 100% of EUV lithography and 85 to 92% of DUV lithography (Canon about 5%, Nikon about 1%), inside a margin-first oligopoly in wafer-fab equipment in which the top five suppliers hold more than 70%. No competitor that prices for economic return cut prices in the 2023 to 2024 digestion: ASML's company-basis gross margin was 51.3% in both years.

Market share consolidates toward ASML mechanically, because each new node raises three barriers: R&D cost (about 4.8 billion EUR a year), optical complexity (Zeiss SMT, 24.9% owned and financed by ASML) and customer co-dependence (the 2012 co-investment tied TSMC, Samsung and Intel to ASML's development cadence).

The only competitors that do not price for return are state-backed Chinese entrants, and they are confined to China's mature nodes. Shanghai Aishengna is expected to make about five immersion tools in 2026 and 20 in 2027, at 10 to 20% yields and 10 to 30 wafers an hour against ASML's roughly 200. The structural fragility is the reinforcing loop between a domestic Chinese tool and a US ban, which acts over three to five years.

Business model: six reinforcing moats, and an installed base that never shrinks. The six moats are technology, the upstream optical lock-in, the integration of more than 100,000 components into one system, switching costs and holistic lithography, scale, and regulation. ASML ties its pricing to customers' productivity rather than to scarcity, so customers accept price increases while placing more orders (customer satisfaction is 88%).

Because the installed base never shrinks, installed-base revenue is a structural grower with a cyclical software component. Service fees run at about 5% of an EUV system's average selling price a year, and lifetime service is worth up to 130% of the tool's value. Installed-base revenue was 8.2 billion EUR in 2025 and is about 12.2 billion EUR in 2026.

ASML sells directly. The only intermediaries are the banks that factor customers' down payments (6.2 billion EUR of receivables were derecognised in FY2025); the factoring accelerates cash but adds a small fragility to credit conditions.

Financial profile: above average on every output test, with weaknesses of shape rather than level.

  • Lumpy cash: annual cash conversion is about 88%, but quarterly free cash flow swings from deeply negative to several times net income, because it follows the timing of down payments.
  • Heavy working capital: 54.8% of trailing revenue at Q3 2026, with a cash-conversion cycle of about 300 days against an ambition below 200.
  • Customers' money: contract liabilities of about 24.6 billion EUR mean that much of the cash belongs to customers.
  • Untested downside: a revenue decline has never tested operating leverage at today's cost base; in the flat years 2022 and 2024, EBIT was flat.

Management: top-quartile among global equipment operators, with two qualifications. The chief executive, Christophe Fouquet (since April 2024), is execution-focused. His record is the beat-and-raise sequence, the capacity decisions, the completed price reset and High-NA in production at Intel (more than one million wafers, availability near 90%), with one material early miss: the October 2024 guidance cut, after which the shares fell 16% in a day. Pay is restrained (chief executive 7.0 million EUR, less than half of US peers), and alignment is strong (no insider selling in twelve months; the long-term incentive is 35% relative total shareholder return and 35% return on average invested capital). The Supervisory Board is fully independent, and PwC's first-year audit is clean.

The first qualification is that communication is deliberately incomplete on the variables that decide 2027 to 2028. The second is that capital return is led by cash rather than by value: ASML bought back 0.4 billion EUR of shares in the 2024 digestion at lower prices, and 6 billion EUR in nine months of 2026 near the highs.

Counter-case. Four customers are 61% of revenue, and Taiwan and Korea are about two-thirds of system sales. The annual report says ASML would "cease to conduct business" if Zeiss supply stopped. Pricing meets a substitute at High-NA: TSMC defers High-NA to about 2030 on cost of ownership and is choosing Low-NA multi-patterning for its A14 node. And in a 2029 downturn, ASML's decremental margin should be read as higher than KLA's, not lower, because ASML carries a larger and newer manufacturing and supplier footprint built for 110-plus systems.

What would change my view. Evidence that Chinese domestic immersion tools reach production-worthy yields before 2029; a second sole-source scare (helium, rare earths, a sanctioned German supplier) that actually stops output; or customer pushback on pricing that is visible in order deferrals rather than in words.

Against the market. I do not disagree with the market on the quality of the franchise. Bernstein notes that ASML's premium to US semiconductor-equipment peers has disappeared for the first time, and I agree that the loss of the premium is a mispricing of structure. I weight the cash-led buyback behaviour more negatively than the market does, because it means capital return falls exactly when the shares would be cheap.

92Score: 92, set by the Rater. None of the four parts is ordinary: 100% of EUV and 85-92% of DUV inside a margin-first oligopoly, six reinforcing moats with pricing tied to productivity and held through two downturns, ROIC 43% (98th percentile) and ROE 50% (97th) with net cash, and new capital (customer-funded capacity) earning far above its cost; the 51.6% gross margin (76th percentile) understates a margin already rising to about 56%. The financial profile, structure and moat are stronger than Avanza's, held from the very top by cyclical predictability (2001 and 2009 gross-margin collapses), four customers at 61% of revenue, a sole-source Zeiss link and a fifth of revenue under policy risk, and by management's deliberately incomplete disclosure (groups 90/93/90/80).

#4 Conservatism of guidance, expectations management, delivery record

Conclusion: ASML's guidance is conservative, specific and recently reliable. Management keeps expectations low by withholding the three numbers the market most wants, and its record of raising guidance and estimates in an up-cycle is strong. The two cuts in four years came at turning points, and the prepaid 2027 order book does not resemble either of them.

Evidence: a record of beats, and a long-range framework that is stale on every line. FY2026 guidance and consensus now coincide (44 to 45 billion EUR of revenue, about 56% gross margin), because consensus followed each of the three raises. The Q4 2026 revenue guide was about 5% above consensus at the midpoint, and the Q4 installed-base guide (about 3.7 billion EUR) 23% above.

Revenue beat the guided midpoint by 2.3 to 2.9% in each of the four quarters to Q1 2026, and beat consensus by 5.4% in Q2 2026. In Q3 2026, revenue was in line, gross margin was 140 basis points above consensus and underlying EPS about 9% above. The Q3 beat came from installed-base revenue, about 400 million EUR above guide, while system sales were about 5% below.

The 2030 framework set in November 2024 (44 to 60 billion EUR of revenue; 56 to 60% gross margin; installed-base revenue of 11 to 13 billion EUR) is now stale on every line. FY2026 sits at its revenue floor, FY2027 consensus near its ceiling, and FY2028 consensus about 23% above its ceiling; installed-base revenue is already at the top of its 2030 range in 2026. The Capital Markets Day on 10 June 2027 is the dated reset.

The record is not unbroken: ASML made two externally driven cuts in four years (July 2022 on supply; October 2024 on customer push-outs), both at turning points.

Inference. ASML's pattern is a conservative opening guide on known items, followed by staged raises as evidence arrives (orders, down payments). Management pairs that pattern with expansive qualitative commentary ("supply below demand through at least 2028"; 2029 to 2030 orders under discussion) and with deliberate silence on the numbers that would let the market verify the ambition. That is proactive expectations management of a particular kind: it keeps the formal bar low while talking up the duration of the cycle to defend the multiple.

So what for the window. The FY2027 range given on 27 January 2027 is more likely than not (about 60%) to have a midpoint below consensus revenue of 57.5 billion EUR. A range of about 52 to 58 billion EUR, with gross margin of 56 to 58%, would be consistent with the company's habit and with our base (56.0 billion EUR; 57.6%). The same habit in January 2026 (a range of 34 to 39 billion EUR) preceded a 22% raise.

What Richard should weigh on 27 January

Not the midpoint of the FY2027 range, but four other numbers: the floor of the range; the annual backlog; the installed-base guide (at least 13.5 billion EUR supports our 14.2 billion); and the Q1 revenue guide (above about 13 billion EUR confirms the upward lean). I put the probability of a raise to the FY2027 range during 2027 at about 70%, with my central expectation +3 to +6% at the midpoint from installed-base revenue and price, since units cannot move. I put the probability of a cut inside the window at about one in six (policy, supply or a pause in upgrades).

Counter-case. The closest comparable for 2027 to 2028 is 2021 to 2022: a supply-constrained ramp in which ASML beat on demand, but supply forced a guidance cut and fast shipments deferred 2.8 billion EUR of revenue. The variables that caused past misses (customer push-outs, supply disruption) are mitigated now, by down payments with exit costs and by 2027 output not being raised beyond what long-lead parts allow. But ASML is setting its 2028 ambition before its suppliers have proven they can deliver it: module build in Wilton and Taiwan, a sole-source mechatronics supplier, and VAT valve lead times of nine months.

What would change my view. A January guide with a midpoint at or above consensus, which would break the habit and would itself signal an internal plan well above 58 billion EUR; or a Q1 revenue guide below 12.5 billion EUR, which would be a real rather than a seasonal softening.

Against the market. The market, and the evidence of past share-price reactions, says bookings matter more than the opening guide on the day: in January 2024 the guide was 5% below consensus and the shares rose 9% on an order beat of 165%. I agree, and I add that this January the market will see an official backlog for the first time in two years, so the print carries unusually high information in both directions.

76Score: 76, set by the Rater. Revenue beat the guided midpoint in every quarter since early 2025, FY2026 guidance was raised three times (+22% at the midpoint), the Q4 guide sits above consensus and the 2030 framework is stale on every line, while the habit of a low opening guide keeps the formal bar beatable. But FY2026 guidance and consensus now coincide, the October 2024 cut (shares -16% in a day) falls inside the two-to-three-year window, and the numbers that decide 2028 are withheld, so it sits just below Indus's raise and above Kerry's steady band, coherent with the guidance group's 74.

#5 Pricing power, operating leverage, cost control and feedback loops

Conclusion: ASML's business model converts revenue growth into outsized profit growth through demonstrated pricing power and a 57 to 61% drop-through, with no financial leverage and little cost-out. Its reinforcing loops front-load the gains into 2026 to 2028 and then turn in a predictable order, which the cash line will show before the P&L does.

Pricing power: demonstrated, not assumed.

  • EUV average selling prices have risen about 5% a year with minimal resistance: about 1 million EUR for each wafer an hour of throughput gained.
  • NXE:3800 pricing rose 5 to 8% on optics upgrades.
  • The step from the NXE:3800E to the 3800F carries a price increase of 20 to 30% for about 13% more throughput: the clearest sign that value-based pricing is already in the price list for new models.
  • Replacement-parts prices in Korea rise 10% from January 2027, reportedly accepted by Samsung and SK hynix.
  • ASML has given no hardware discounts on EUV through two downturns.

In our base, like-for-like price adds about 3.5 points to FY2027 revenue growth and about 4 points to FY2028 (about 1.6 billion and 3.8 billion EUR cumulative), at close to full margin. The 3800F adds a further 3 to 4 points a year of EUV mix. Price is therefore about one-seventh of FY2028 revenue growth but about a quarter of FY2028 gross-profit growth.

Pricing power has four limits: resets are explicitly not annual; High-NA pricing meets multi-patterning as a cheaper route; DUV pricing in China faces local tools; and management says part of the gain funds capacity.

Operating leverage: high on the way up, and higher on the way down. Operating expenses of about 6.2 billion EUR (R&D about 4.8 billion, SG&A about 1.5 billion) are genuinely fixed over two years: ASML did not cut R&D in 2009 or in 2023 to 2024. Incremental revenue dropped through to EBIT at about 61% in FY2026, and the base carries 57% in FY2027 and FY2028. At a 45% EBIT margin, a 10% change in revenue moves EBIT by 12 to 14%, and a 5% revenue miss concentrated in upgrades costs about 9% of EBIT.

Of the 5.5 points of EBIT-margin gain from FY2026 to FY2028, about 2.9 points come from operating-expense leverage and 2.6 points from gross margin. The source of the gain shifts from margin, led by software upgrades in 2026, to volume and price in 2027 to 2028.

The leverage is asymmetric. A revenue fall would bring a mix shift (fewer upgrades, and under-absorbed capacity built for 110-plus units) that makes the decremental margin 65 to 75%. In a flat year, fixed-cost absorption turns from about +0.5 points of gross margin to about -0.5 points.

Drop-through on the way up: about 61% in FY2026, 57% in FY2027 and FY2028.

Decremental margin on the way down: 65 to 75%, because a fall brings fewer upgrades and idle capacity.

Financial leverage: none, and none planned. Net cash is about 13 billion EUR at end-2026 and rises to about 18 to 20 billion EUR by 2028 to 2029, after buybacks of 13 billion and 17 billion EUR in 2027 and 2028. Net financial items add about 0.5 to 0.75 billion EUR a year. Only two items below EBIT matter: the tax rate after the innovation-box ruling expires at end-2028 (each point of tax is about 1.2% of EPS), and the falling share count (about +2 points a year to EPS growth).

Cost-out: small, and later than announced. Engineering hiring and the retention-award expense absorb the delayering's gross saving of about 100 to 200 million EUR a year from May 2027. In a downturn, ASML could remove within a year perhaps 0.5 to 0.8 billion EUR of operating expenses (8 to 12%) and 1 to 1.5 billion EUR of capital spending and supplier advances. Those savings are worth one to two points of EBIT margin, against the four to six points that a downturn's mix shift would remove. The efficiency gains that will reach the accounts are in working capital (each point of trade working capital is about 0.7 billion EUR of cash at FY2028 revenue) and in cost of goods per unit, not in operating expenses.

Feedback loops, and the order in which they turn. Four loops reinforce ASML's results today:

  • The installed-base flywheel is the floor: it adds about 1 billion EUR of high-margin revenue a year, whatever happens to upgrades.
  • The upgrade-for-cleanroom loop earns near-100%-margin revenue while customers cannot get tools or cleanroom space; Jefferies credits it with about 400 basis points of 2026 gross-margin expansion.
  • The prepayment-to-capital-return loop uses down payments of 35 to 40% to fund inventory, supplier advances and buybacks.
  • The lead-time-to-booking loop is damped by ASML's controls; its failure mode is push-outs, not cancellations.

One loop works against ASML slowly but carries the risk of a sudden step: China's substitution of domestic tools. The two reinforcing loops that will turn inside the horizon turn in a known order: upgrades first (late 2027 to 2028, acting on installed-base growth and gross-margin mix), then prepayments (2029, acting on free cash flow and buybacks a year before the P&L). The AI-financing loop is external to ASML and is the trigger for both.

Counter-case: upgrades are cyclical and can reverse fast. Jefferies argues that the upgrade component reverses when tightness eases, leaving 2028 gross margin flat at 58.2%, or at 55.2% if upgrades fall. The 2023 precedent shows how fast: ASML cut installed-base guidance from +5% to flat inside two quarters when utilisation fell, and quarterly installed-base revenue fell from 1.6 billion EUR in Q4 2023 to 1.3 billion EUR in Q1 2024. Morgan Stanley and Bernstein take the resilient side: the 3800E upgrade cycle is early, and upgrades bypass hardware lead times. No broker quantifies how far upgrades fall when cleanrooms open, and no precedent exists at this scale.

What would change my view. On pricing: a FY2027 gross-margin guide above 58% (more than half of the reset flowing through) or at or below 57% (less than half). On the loops: a sequential fall of more than 20% in installed-base revenue in Q1 2027.

Against the market. The market has the pricing story and the upgrade debate. It does not have three things: the sequence (upgrades, then down payments, then units), the asymmetry of the operating leverage, and the point that in 2029 EPS, free cash flow and the order signal can move in three different directions.

80Score: 80, set by the Rater. Three gears are proven: pricing power (EUV ASPs about +5% a year with no hardware discounts through two downturns, 3800F priced 20-30% higher for 13% more throughput, Korean parts +10% accepted), fixed operating expenses with a 57-61% drop-through, and reinforcing loops (installed-base service, near-100%-margin upgrades, prepayments funding capacity and buybacks), lifting EBIT margin from 34.6% to about 47% by FY2028. The forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio is only about 1.4x on FY2026-30 because the margin is already high and FY2029 pauses, there is no financial leverage, cost-out is small and the gearing is asymmetric (65-75% decremental margin in a fall), so it is held below the 90 level, which needs financial leverage too; level with the strongest scored model (Helios Towers 80).

#6 Forecast financials

Conclusion: the forecasts describe the strongest earnings phase in ASML's history: EPS triples in three years on a 29% revenue compound growth rate and 13 points of margin. The shape of the phase is more predictable than its length: traceable to FY2028, a pause in FY2029 that could be a decline, and a cash line that turns before the earnings do.

Decomposition, FY2025 to FY2028: a high-quality composition. Revenue does about two-thirds of the work in tripling EPS, margin about 28% and buybacks about 5%, while items below EBIT subtract about 1%. The composition is high quality because it needs no help from tax, interest or one-offs. Low-NA units and pricing deliver more than half of the 37 billion EUR revenue step; within installed-base revenue, upgrades contribute about 3.8 billion EUR of the step and service about 3.0 billion EUR.

Scope for double-digit growth, and for higher growth and margins than in the past. The forecast is a step-change against FY2019 to FY2025 on every line. Through FY2028 the arithmetic is unusually traceable: units are capped and largely ordered, prices are signed, operating expenses are fixed, there is no leverage, tax is neutral, and buybacks are sized to cash. FY2029 is the first year with a genuine probability of digestion, and the base treats FY2029 as a pause; FY2030 growth resumes at 10%.

Where the base sits against consensus, and why. Our EBIT margins match consensus in every year (44.8% against 44.9% in FY2027; 47.2% against 47.0% in FY2028). Our revenue is 2.6% below consensus for FY2027 and 5.4% below for FY2028, on China DUV and High-NA timing. Our EPS is only 2.8% and 1.7% below, because larger buybacks offset part of the revenue gap.

Our FY2029 EPS is 15% below a thin consensus that carries +13.5% revenue growth and rests on four to eight brokers; consensus's FY2029 gross-profit figure, identical to its FY2028 figure, is an artefact. The broker range for FY2028 EPS is about 53 to 90 EUR (Morgan Stanley 68.5, Bernstein 84, Redburn about 91): the market's own measure of how much hangs on three numbers.

My lean on the base: up for FY2027, down for FY2028 and FY2029, but no input changed. I lean FY2027 EPS up modestly (+2 to +4%): upgrades have beaten in every quarter of 2026, pricing is signed, and the Q1 2027 seasonal input (-15% from Q4) is at the severe end of the precedent range of -10% to -16%. I lean FY2028 down on units (the 2022 supply precedent) and neutral on margin, and FY2029 down on the base rate of digestion. I change no input: the base already sits below consensus on revenue, and leaning it further would double-count the conservatism that the January guide will supply.

Scenarios beside the base, with my probabilities. Every scenario except the upside lowers FY2028 EPS.

Counter-case. Consensus's bulls (Bernstein, Redburn and Deutsche Bank, at 83 to 91 EUR for FY2028) argue that 110 systems is not a supply cap, that de-bottlenecking and AI-assisted cycle-time reduction can deliver 35 to 40% growth in system sales, and that the 1c DRAM super-cycle extends the up-cycle. If the bulls are right, the base is about 10% too low in FY2028 and the 2029 pause is wrong.

What would change my view. The January backlog (above about 50 billion EUR supports 2028 at 110-plus units; below 45 billion EUR argues for fewer); the Q1 2027 installed-base print; the 2028 unit number and gross-margin framework at the Capital Markets Day; and non-current contract liabilities through H2 2027, for the 2029 question.

Against the market. Consensus FY2027 is roughly right, and I would not build a case on beating it. Consensus FY2028 is the battleground, and I sit 2% below it. Consensus FY2029 is too high and will come down as coverage widens; the market may read that fall as a cut, although much of it will be an artefact of coverage.

93Score: 93, set by the Rater. About 22% sits well inside the 15-30% A band and is honest: organic, no tax or interest help, buybacks only about 2 points a year, with EBIT margin moving into a 45-48% band against a 31-35% past and consensus EPS growth at the 92nd percentile. Placed in the upper part of the band rather than the top because the growth is front-loaded (+34%, +34%, then a FY2029 pause the memo puts at 40% odds of a decline) and FY2030 has no consensus behind it.

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Conclusion: the scope for upgrades is real but modest for FY2027 (+3 to +6% by October 2027), large but binary for FY2028 to FY2030 at the June 2027 Capital Markets Day, and almost certain for the long-range framework. The case is favourably exposed to guidance, neutral on near-term consensus, and modestly favourable on the narrative.

Guidance: up in substance, down in form. Current guidance sits far below what we and the market expect: FY2026 sits at the 2030 framework's floor, there is no FY2027 number yet, and FY2028 consensus exceeds the framework's ceiling by about a quarter. The pattern of staged raises is intact, so guidance will move up in substance over the window. The cost is in form: the two opening guides inside the window (January 2027 and January 2028) will each have a midpoint below consensus, and each will give the market a chance to read a peak into a floor.

Estimates: FY2027 held in a band, FY2028 decided at the Capital Markets Day. Consensus FY2027 EPS will most likely be held in a band of 55 to 60 EUR: a 2 to 4% revenue trim after January, offset in EPS by installed-base revenue and margin, then +3 to +6% after the July and October 2027 prints as pricing and upgrades show in the margin. Consensus FY2028 is the line that moves, and the Capital Markets Day decides its direction.

The 2030 framework: replaced with near certainty (about 90%). At the Capital Markets Day I expect:

  • revenue scenarios of roughly 65 to 90 billion EUR for 2030, against our FY2030 of 78.8 billion EUR;
  • a gross-margin range reaching about 60% at the top;
  • an installed-base ambition above 20 billion EUR;
  • a new or enlarged buyback, because the current 12 billion EUR programme runs out around mid-2027 at the current pace.

Narrative: thin in five places, three of which can move in our favour. The sell-side narrative already carries most of our dynamics: 2028 units, pricing, the cyclicality of upgrades, the MATCH Act, High-NA timing and the de-rating playbook. Over six to twelve months, three thin places can move in our favour:

  • the official backlog in January, which would convert Bernstein's inferred 56 billion EUR into fact;
  • the 2028 and 2030 numbers at the Capital Markets Day, which would convert the capacity debate into a plan;
  • the evidence on upgrade mix through 2027: if installed-base revenue holds above 3.5 billion EUR a quarter through H1, Jefferies' flat-margin case loses its anchor.

Two thin places can move against us: the probability of a 2029 decline, and the turn in cash before earnings, which no broker models.

So what. The case does not need sell-side upgrades inside the window to work, because the multiple already discounts a peak that the fundamentals have not reached. Richard should treat the January print as the event that protects FY2028 consensus (through the backlog), even if it trims FY2027, and the Capital Markets Day as the single largest revision event in either direction.

Counter-case: brokers have stopped raising fair values. Target-price revisions have stalled (+1% in one month after +42% in six), the first sign that brokers are no longer raising fair values with their estimates. The share of Buy ratings (76%) has fallen four points in three months and is more likely to fall toward 70% than to rise, because ASML is a crowded consensus holding. The dissenters (Jefferies, Hold at 1,590 EUR; AlphaValue, Underweight at 1,472 EUR) argue against the cycle, not against the company.

What would change my view. A FY2027 installed-base guide below 13.5 billion EUR in January, which would mean the upgrade loop is turning before pricing lands; or a 2030 central scenario at the Capital Markets Day below our 78.8 billion EUR.

Against the market. The market expects the Capital Markets Day to raise the framework and is arguing about the amount. I agree. I put the probability that the new central scenario is set above our FY2030 revenue at about 50%, and above thin consensus FY2029 at about 35%, because management reiterates frameworks rather than stretching them: in November 2024 it held the range unchanged a month after the guidance cut.

62Score: 62, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, is likely raised in substance: about 70% odds of a +3-6% raise to the FY2027 range during 2027 and near-certain replacement of the stale 2030 framework at the June 2027 CMD, but the January opening guide is about 60% likely to sit below consensus, and a 4-5% raise on 25% revenue growth is only about 0.2 on Richard's ratio. Consensus FY2027 is likely held in a 55-60 EUR band, FY2028 is binary at the CMD, FY2029 consensus is too high, and the narrative is only modestly favourable with target revisions stalling, so it sits between Helios Towers' small serial raises and Teqnion, matching the group's 62.

ASML's momentum profile is therefore the sector's, and the sector's regime decides whether the favourable guidance gap is paid for inside the window or after it.

Tokyo Electron raised its fiscal 2027 growth guidance for new equipment to 59%, and Lam, KLA and Applied all call calendar 2027 wafer-fab-equipment spending above 200 billion USD.

The peer basket explains about 62% of ASML's share price on a rolling six months, and ASML's beta has fallen from 1.45 to 0.76. ASML has become the low-beta way to own the theme, which cushions the shares on the way down and caps them on the way up.

Inference. The gap between A on estimates and D on technicals reflects the market's fear about financing and the peak, not a demand signal, and the gap belongs to the sector, not to ASML alone. ASML's de-rating is company-specific in origin: its earnings outran its price by more than any peer's, so its multiple sits at a lower percentile of its own history (the 32nd of ten years, against ASM International's 45th and VAT's 68th). The de-rating is sector-specific in cause: the market refuses to capitalise the 2028 peak.

So what. A change in the sector regime (credit spreads narrowing, Semiconductors moving off Underweight) would lift ASML through its shared component, whatever its own news. The January backlog and the June unit number move the remaining, company-specific third of the share price. In the next three months the dated events cluster on the negative side (the 10 November expiries, the December defence bill, and monthly memory-price data near the expected peak in price growth), which is consistent with the current D reading.

Counter-case. Momentum investors would say that the D on technicals is the signal and the A on estimates the lag. In 2017 to 2018, estimates kept rising for fourteen months after the multiple peaked; in 2021 to 2022, the stock de-rated 27% from its November 2021 peak before revenue peaked.

What would change my view. The 200-day average turning down after rising for twelve months would mark a change of technical regime. A return of the Buy share above 80% would mark crowding at the top. Positive FY2028 revisions turning to cuts after January would be the first fundamental confirmation of the bears' case.

Against the market. The market reads the technical break as information about demand; I read it as information about financing and positioning. I agree with the market that the stock is crowded, and that a disappointment on the 2028 number would meet few marginal buyers.

80Score: 80, set by the Rater. Both measures sit in the top fifth on their last readings, but A needs no part negative and technical momentum is D (below the 50- and 100-day averages, 19% off the high, and since then below the 200-day) with the sector Underweight and the Buy share down four points, so B. Placed in the upper half of the band because guidance (three raises, Q4 above consensus) and revisions (+9% three months, 88th percentile; +38% six months, 96th) are strongly positive and the weakness is shared by every front-end peer, with the 200-day still rising.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

Conclusion: the case is simple, and its 18-month forecasts are among the most predictable in the European universe. But ASML is a cyclical with a quarter of revenue under policy risk, a share price three-fifths driven by its sector, and a FY2028 to FY2029 range of outcomes that is wide and skewed down. Riskiness is therefore low on fundamentals in the near term, and high on perception and over the three-year horizon.

Simplicity: a virtue for 18 months, a fragility after. The case is simple to state and to track. Three numbers (2028 Low-NA units, the flow-through of the price reset, and the upgrade run-rate) plus China policy decide it. The transmission from ASML's plan to EPS is arithmetical in five of seven links (units stated, operating expenses guided, tax known, share count sized to cash); only the price percentage and the upgrade share of installed-base revenue must be inferred. Simplicity is a virtue for the next 18 months, because two of the three numbers are contracted, and a fragility for months 18 to 36, because none of them is.

The range of outcomes, stated plainly. For FY2027, the 80% range for EPS is 50 to 61 EUR around 56 EUR (about -11% to +9%), and for revenue 52 to 59 billion EUR. I put the probability that FY2027 EPS lands at or above the base at about 60%, at or above consensus at about 45%, and the probability that FY2027 revenue lands within 5% of the base at about 70%. For FY2028, the range is 57 to 87 EUR around 75 EUR (-24% to +16%), skewed down. For FY2029, it is 60 to 95 EUR, with about 40% on a decline. For a cyclical capital-goods company, these ranges are unusually narrow near term and ordinary further out.

Fragilities: two unproven strengths and two untested assumptions.

Strengths the FY2028 case needs that ASML has not yet shown. A third consecutive year of unit growth above 30%, with the installation workforce to match: 2019 to 2021 produced two such years, and the third, 2022, ended in a supply-driven cut. And gross-margin expansion during a capacity ramp: gross margin fell in the 2017 and 2022 ramps, and the first NXE:3300 systems carried zero gross margin.

Assumptions no cycle has tested at this scale. How far upgrades fall when cleanroom tightness ends. And whether re-allocating banned Chinese immersion tools works at the scale of a whole country: ASML has done it once, at small scale, in late 2023.

Share-price risks: the fundamental risks are mostly slow; the perception risks are fast.

Kind of riskSpeed and trackabilityExamples
Fundamental, slowTrackable: units quarterly, installed-base revenue guided quarterly, region mix, non-current contract liabilities as the order proxy, the backlog once a yearUnits, upgrades, mix, orders
Fundamental, fastSudden; dated triggers tomorrow and in DecemberA China ban by decree
Catastrophic, low probabilitySuddenTaiwan (25.5% of 2025 sales; 32% of Q3 2026 system sales); a Zeiss or TRUMPF outage
PerceptionFast, frequent and material whatever the fundamentals; each can move the shares 10 to 20%, and the sector regime amplifies themAI-financing read-across (CoreWeave bonds, hyperscaler spreads, Oracle and SoftBank); memory-price prints; China tool headlines (the July 2026 DUV announcement cut ASML's shares about 7% and the sector's value by about 1 trillion USD); the sector's habit of de-rating before the peak

62% of the share price's variance is explained by the peer basket: the P&L is predictable and the share price is not.

Sector and cyclical risk, with precedents. Semiconductor-equipment multiples compress 40 to 50% from their peak, three to six months before the revenue peak. In Deutsche Bank's 2022 study, the compression lasted 79 weeks on average, and consensus cuts lagged the price peak by about 37 weeks. ASML's own multiple went from about 29x to 15x in 2017 to 2018, and from 47x to about 20x in 2021 to 2022. In the two hard downturns (2001 and 2009), gross margin compressed about 20 points within three quarters of the utilisation peak. Those precedents belong to the back half of the model, not to the next 18 months, because customers have prepaid 2027 deliveries.

ASML has already been through most of a cycle's compression (about 40x to 20x) while estimates have not yet peaked. The sector's own rule of thumb calls that configuration a debate worth buying into, provided the feared peak year keeps being planned up.

Where the share-price downside sits: in 2028 estimates, not in the multiple. On unchanged consensus earnings, the multiple is already near its trough, so the downside from the multiple alone is about 8 to 17%, depending on how the forward earnings roll. Larger falls need consensus earnings to fall: a plateau (FY2028 EPS about 60 EUR) at 18x gives about 1,080 EUR (-23%); the MATCH case at 20 to 24x gives about 880 to 1,050 EUR (-25 to -37%); and the full-cycle bear gives about 750 EUR (-47%).

Counter-case. Simplicity cuts both ways. BESI's single driver produced a 54% drawdown when one adoption date slipped while earnings held. ASML has three drivers and two key customer countries, not the seven categories and the service cushion of 23% of revenue that Applied has. And the correlated tails (a financing freeze, a memory break and a ban all landing in the same year) make the joint downside larger than the separate probabilities suggest.

What would change my view. Any of the five observables in the judgements section. For riskiness specifically, a change in disclosure (quarterly bookings restored, or the split of installed-base revenue given) would lower riskiness by a grade.

Against the market. The market scores ASML's risk by its beta and its sector. I score it by its drivers, and find the next 18 months low-risk on fundamentals and high-risk on perception, which is the opposite of how the shares are trading.

57Score: 57, set by the Rater. The case is simple and the next year narrow for a cyclical: FY2027 EPS cone about -11% to +9% on contracted units and signed prices, net cash, everything below EBIT mechanical, and fundamental drivers trackable quarterly. Against that sit a sudden policy binary on about a fifth of revenue with dated triggers, a FY2028 cone of -24% to +16% skewed down, a 40% chance of a 2029 decline, correlated financing, memory and ban tails, and a share price 62% explained by its sector with 10-20% perception moves, so it sits just above NKT's backlog-visible but execution-exposed case and below Banca Generali (groups 55 and 68).

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

Conclusion: the stock's fundamentals are in a Reinforcing phase that has at least five more quarters to run, while its price is already in the digestion the sector applies before a peak. Whether the phase broadens into 2029 or stalls there is the question that January and June will answer.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule places the stock in the Reinforcing phase: guidance raised three times, estimates up 79% in a year, visibility extended from 2027 to 2028 and beyond, High-NA moved from doubt to production, and margins at records. The share price, by contrast, is in a digestion: 19% below the high (more since), technicals D, the multiple at the bottom of its range, the Buy share falling from a crowded level, and the sector Underweight.

Inference. The fundamentals are reinforcing, while the share price is behaving as if the thesis were stalling. The two can coexist for a while in this sector, as in 2017 to 2018, when estimates rose for fourteen months while the multiple fell. The divergence resolves in one of two ways. Either estimates peak and the price was right (the 2018 and 2022 outcomes), or visibility extends past the feared peak and the price catches up (the outcomes after the late-2022 Capital Markets Day and in early 2024, when a re-rating followed the order book). The decisive evidence is whether 2028 keeps being planned up and whether 2029 can be shown to be a growth year; the January backlog and the June Capital Markets Day are where that evidence arrives.

So what. The honest label is "reinforcing fundamentals inside a de-rating". The thesis is broadening on earnings (memory is now about half of system sales, pricing is a new leg, and the installed base is a capacity product), while the market pre-positions for stalling. In Richard's six-phase language, I would call the fundamentals reinforcing, with a 40% probability of moving to stalling in 2029 and a small probability of collapsing in a year of correlated tails. The stock is not bottoming, because nothing has gone wrong, and not turning up, because nothing needs to recover. The de-rating has done to the multiple the work a bottoming phase does, without any damage to the earnings.

Counter-case. Jefferies reads the stock as stalling in all but name: the semiconductor revenue cycle peaks in Q4 2026 on base effects, equipment names de-rate further in the medium term despite record orders, and earnings upgrades will not drive the price until the capacity question resolves. If 2029 is a decline, Jefferies will have been right about the phase and early by a year.

What would change my view. Toward stalling: falling non-current contract liabilities, a miss on installed-base revenue, or a 2028 unit number at or below 110. Toward a longer Reinforcing phase: 2029 to 2030 orders converting with down payments during 2027, or a 2030 central scenario above 80 billion EUR at the Capital Markets Day.

Against the market. The dashboard rule and I agree on Reinforcing; the market's price says stalling. My probability-weighted view sits between the two and nearer the dashboard: the phase is reinforcing for at least the next five quarters, and the question is 2029, not 2027.

64Score: 64, set by the Rater. The memo's and the computed Reinforcing are right, with broadening elements (memory now about half of system sales, a new pricing leg, IBM as a capacity product) and at least five more quarters of contracted improvement, but the step-up is already in consensus (FY2027 EPS +79% in a year), the price is in a sector de-rating with technicals D, and 2029 carries a 40% chance of stalling. That is mid Reinforcing, behind Kuehne + Nagel's early reinforcing and level with Tenaris's reinforcing on pricing, above Nexans's paused momentum.

#11 The fair multiple

Conclusion: the guideline's 29.4x is the right multiple for a stock in peak delivery and the wrong one to apply to earnings for a year we model as flat. My central fair multiple is therefore about 26x (between the median and the 75th percentile), with 29.4x the bull outcome if the June 2027 Capital Markets Day shows 2029 to be a growth year, and 20x the bear if the order book turns.

The guideline: the 90th percentile of ASML's own ten-year range, 29.38x. Viewforth's guideline for a stock in the Reinforcing phase is the 90th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history of two-year-forward P/E. The model applies 29.38x to the two-year-forward EPS at the 18-month valuation date (about 81.5 EUR, three-quarters FY2029 and one-quarter FY2030).

Today's multiple sits at or near the bottom of every version of its own range. The model measures today's multiple at 20.1x on its own two-year-forward EPS (about 70 EUR, three-quarters FY2028 and one-quarter FY2027). The financials block's five-year weekly series puts it at 19.7x, the 2nd percentile of five years. At 1,250 EUR, it is about 19x. The different series differ only by the roll of EPS and the date, and none changes the conclusion; the end notes reconcile them. The re-rating leg in #12 (20.1x to 29.4x, +46%) is measured on the model's own basis throughout.

History: ASML has never held a 90th-percentile multiple into a year of flat growth. ASML has traded at 29x or above only in three periods: the zero-interest-rate peak (November 2020 to December 2021, 30.9x to 39.8x); two short bursts in 2024 (February to March, and June, at about 30x); and this cycle's upgrade phase (October 2025; January to February 2026 at 31.8x; May to June 2026 at 31.0x to 35.2x). In 2018 the multiple fell to 15x as growth slowed from 33% to 22%; in 2022 it fell to about 20x as supply capped growth. Morgan Stanley's reading, that the stock troughs at 18 to 22x two-year-forward earnings in down-cycles and that 22 to 25x is the instructive mid-cycle range, matches the ten-year bands.

My view: the guideline is right about the delivery and wrong about the date. The guideline's logic, that a stock in peak delivery deserves the top of its range, is sound. But by 31 March 2028, when the model applies the multiple, the market will be looking at FY2029 (our base +4% EPS, with a 40% chance of a decline) and FY2030. ASML's multiple has never stayed at its 90th percentile when the next twelve months' growth was in single digits; it has gone to its median or below. Weighting the three states gives about 25x; I round my central fair multiple to 26x, between the median and the 75th percentile, with 29.4x as the bull outcome and 20x as the bear. A second argument supports a multiple below the guideline: the premium to US semiconductor-equipment peers that justified the top of ASML's range has disappeared. ASML now trades at a discount of 4 to 7% to the group, against a premium of 40 to 100% in 2014 to 2022, and restoring the premium needs the market to believe again in the lithography-intensity and High-NA story, which is a 2028 to 2030 event.

Counter-case for the guideline. Three brokers already apply multiples at or above the guideline to the same horizon: Deutsche Bank uses 26x 2028 EPS (a 20% premium to peers), Redburn 25x two-year-forward EV/EBIT for a 2,100 EUR target, and Bernstein a mid-cycle 30x twelve-month-forward EPS. If the June Capital Markets Day resets 2030 revenue to 85 to 90 billion EUR, the two-year-forward EPS to which the market applies a multiple in 2028 would also be higher than our 81.5 EUR, and the top of the range would be in play on both legs.

What would change my view. Up to the guideline: 2029 orders with down payments visible in non-current contract liabilities by Q3 2027. Down to the bear: a turn in installed-base revenue in Q1 2027, or enactment of the MATCH Act with a fast timetable.

Against the market. The market applies about 20x; the sell side applies 25 to 30x; the guideline is 29.4x; I apply 26x. The gap between the market and me is the whole case. The gap between the guideline and me is about 300 EUR of share price at the 18-month valuation date, and it does not change the direction of the answer.

82Score: 82, set by the Rater. Cheap on the peer measure and neutral on its own range gives B, with the own-range reading moving towards cheap as the shares fell to about 19x. Placed in the upper half of the band because the cheapness is only partly deserved: a FY2029 pause and the lost premium to US semicap justify a multiple below the 90th-percentile guideline (the memo's own fair 26x), but not today's 20x for a monopoly whose next five quarters are contracted.

#12 Total shareholder return, decomposed

Conclusion: the model's +70% over 18 months and +110% over three years are about two-thirds re-rating and one-third earnings at 18 months, and about half and half at three years. On my central multiple of 26x, the 18-month return is about +52%; the earnings leg alone delivers about +17%; and the plausible bear is a loss of 13 to 22%. The return is skewed strongly to the positive, because the multiple has already compressed while the earnings to March 2028 are largely contracted.

What drives each leg. The multiple leg (+46%) is the move from 20.1x to the 29.38x guideline. It is identical at both horizons, because the model reaches the fair multiple at the 18-month date and holds it. The earnings leg is the move in two-year-forward EPS from about 70 EUR today to about 81.5 EUR at March 2028 (+16%) and about 100 EUR at September 2029 (+42%, on FY2030 EPS of 91.7 EUR and an extrapolated FY2031 near 103 EUR).

The 18-month earnings leg is small for a company whose EPS grows 34% in each of 2027 and 2028, because by March 2028 the forward window rolls onto FY2029, our pause year. The model therefore already charges the case for the digestion in its earnings leg while rewarding it with a peak multiple, which is the internal tension discussed in #11. Dividends add only 1 to 2 points, because the payout ratio is about 20% and ASML returns cash mainly through buybacks, which sit inside the earnings leg as a 2% annual reduction in the share count.

The template's own split, on trailing earnings, tells the same story from the other side. On trailing earnings and the trailing multiple, the split is -2.5% from the multiple and +73.5% from earnings over 18 months, and -7.3% and +124% over three years. Almost all the return is earnings growth that is already in the forecasts, and the trailing multiple barely moves because EPS grows into it. Read together, the two splits say that the case needs no re-rating on trailing earnings to deliver a large return, but needs a re-rating on forward earnings to deliver the model's figure.

Counter-case: the return above the earnings leg needs a re-rating the precedents delay. If the market stays at 20x through the window, the return is +17%: respectable, but not the thesis. And the earnings leg itself assumes that 2029 is flat rather than down. If 2029 is down, the earnings leg is about -8% at the 18-month date, and the multiple leg has to carry everything.

#13 Summary conclusion

ASML is a monopoly at the gate of a customer-funded build-out. Its factory is sold out for 2027; 2028 is largely ordered and prepaid; prices have just been reset upward; an installed base compounds high-margin revenue; and the company has no debt. Management has raised guidance three times this year while refusing to quantify the three numbers that would let the market verify 2028. EPS triples from FY2025 to FY2028 on arithmetic that is unusually traceable.

The share price sits at the bottom of its own ten-year valuation range because the market, following the sector's playbook, has decided to de-rate before a peak it cannot yet see. The case for Richard is therefore not that the earnings will surprise, because they are already in consensus. The case is that the market is applying a trough multiple to a company whose next five quarters are contracted, and whose debate (2028 units, the flow-through of pricing, the upgrade run-rate, and 2029) will be settled on two dates: 27 January and 10 June 2027. The sector's precedents say that a multiple at the 2nd percentile while estimates rise is the configuration that pays, when the feared peak year keeps being planned up.

The risks are real and mostly external to ASML.

  • A statutory China ban: about 8 to 10% of a year's EPS, nearer than the market frames it, but milder.
  • An AI-financing or memory shock, reaching upgrades first and 2028 to 2029 orders second.
  • A 2029 that every ASML precedent says could be a digestion year (40%).
  • A share price three-fifths driven by a sector in a risk-off regime.

The window carries three optical traps that will look like a peak while the fundamentals improve: a conservative January guide, the Q1 2027 step-down, and reported growth falling to single digits by Q4 2027 on base effects. Each trap is a point at which to add to the position, if the backlog, the installed-base guide and non-current contract liabilities hold.

End notes

Price basis. All valuation figures use 1,407.2 EUR, the Master Dashboard's 23 October 2026 close and the price in the Financial Analyst's model. Morgan Stanley's note of 6 November is written at about 1,250 EUR; figures quoted at 1,250 EUR say so.

Forecast basis. Forecasts are the Financial Analyst's model, update 2: EPS of 41.9 / 55.9 / 75.1 / 78.1 / 91.7 EUR for FY2026 to FY2030. Money is in EUR unless stated. EPS is on the model's Viewforth basis, within 2% of the second set's reported-basic cross-check in every year. The summary's "about 25 EUR" for FY2025 EPS rounds the 24.7 EUR used in the Analyst's summary and the 25.4 EUR in the forecast table; the bases differ slightly. FY2026 EPS includes the 509.7 million EUR Mistral AI revaluation gain (about 1.3 EUR a share); the FactSet median (42.49 EUR) appears to include the gain and the mean (41.19 EUR) not. Net cash in the model includes customer down payments: the working-capital input was re-expressed for this, and on the old definition the model wrongly showed net cash falling to 8.8 billion EUR.

Terms. Low-NA EUV is ASML's NXE extreme-ultraviolet platform; High-NA EUV is the EXE platform; DUV is deep-ultraviolet lithography, including immersion tools. Installed-base revenue is ASML's Installed Base Management segment (service, field upgrades and productivity software; IBM in the charts and tables). Contract liabilities are customers' down payments; the non-current part is the memo's proxy for orders beyond the next year. The Capital Markets Day is abbreviated CMD in some charts and in the Rater's notes, wafer-fab equipment WFE, gross margin GM, and average selling price ASP. The 18-month column is the model's valuation date of 31 March 2028; the three-year column is 30 September 2029.

Which multiple is "today's". The model measures 20.1x on its own two-year-forward EPS (about 70 EUR, three-quarters FY2028 and one-quarter FY2027). The financials block's five-year weekly series gives 19.7x (2nd percentile; median 24.9x; 90th percentile 31.4x). The dashboard's series gave 21.8x (32nd percentile of ten years) on 24 October. The Phases page's own "now" of 24.7x (19% below the guideline) is the dashboard series at the end of September, when the shares were 1,595 EUR; at the model's price it is about 21.8x, and at 1,250 EUR about 19x. The bases differ by the roll of EPS and by the date, not by anything that changes the conclusion.

Sources of the visuals. Default charts and tables: the house default-visuals set for ASML-NL from model update 2 (FactSet history and consensus; the Financial Analyst's model summary; the Master Dashboard's price and valuation charts). Charts marked x01 to x07 and the inline diagrams were drawn for this page from figures stated in the memo. The cash-line chart in the summary and the installed-base chart under judgement 2 were drawn by the Copy Editor from the model's figures as stated in #6; service is derived as installed-base revenue less upgrades.

Derived figures. In the judgements matrix, share-price effects apply the memo's rule (one EUR of two-year-forward EPS is about 20 EUR of share price at 20x, 26 EUR at 26x) to the EPS effect shown; they are approximate except for judgements 1 and 5, where the memo states the two-year-forward effect. In the gross-margin bridge, High-NA and ramp costs are the midpoints of their stated ranges, and the "volume, EUV mix and other" bar is a balancing item to reach the model's 58.3%. How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
